stories.headline: OpenAI says ChatGPT ad business hit $1B annualized run rate in about 200 days

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced on Monday, August 31, 2026 that its advertising business reached $1 billion in annualized revenue run rate, calling it proof of a 'diversified business model'.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI on Monday announced that its advertising business has hit $1 billion in annualized revenue run rate, a milestone that the company is touting as proof of its 'diversified business model.'

key_facts.fact: The ad business is roughly 200 days old; OpenAI began testing ads inside ChatGPT in the U.S. in February 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI said Monday that its ad business, which is roughly 200 days old, builds on its existing revenue engines like its enterprise offerings, consumer subscriptions and usage-based application programming interfaces. OpenAI began testing ads within its ChatGPT chatbot in the U.S. in February.

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT ads now run in more than 40 countries, and on Monday OpenAI opened its self-serve ad platform to marketers in India, Europe, the Middle East and North Africa.
key_facts.excerpt: ChatGPT ads have launched in more than 40 countries, with OpenAI opening up its self-serve ad platform on Monday to marketers in India, Europe, the Middle East, and North Africa.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is targeting $2.5 billion in advertising revenue for 2026 — more than double the current pace — while tracking toward overall annualized revenue above $40 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is targeting $2.5 billion in advertising revenue for the current year and is tracking toward annualized revenue exceeding $40 billion, roughly twice its run rate at the end of 2025.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI reported $6.7 billion in second-quarter 2026 revenue, up from $5.7 billion in the prior quarter, and posted a $38.5 billion net loss in 2025 on $13.07 billion of revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI reported $6.7 billion in revenue for the second quarter of 2026, up from $5.7 billion the quarter before. The company posted a net loss of $38.5 billion in 2025 on $13.07 billion in revenue and is working toward a planned 2027 IPO.

key_facts.fact: The company is under pressure to justify an $852 billion valuation ahead of an expected IPO; ads appear only for free-tier users, who make up the vast majority of ChatGPT's 1 billion weekly active users.
key_facts.excerpt: The artificial intelligence company is gearing up for what is expected to be a massive IPO, and is under pressure to justify its $852 billion valuation to investors. ... Ads within [the] chatbot appear for [users on] its free tier, [which] makes up the vast majority of its 1 billion weekly active users

key_facts.fact: India, one of ChatGPT's largest markets by weekly users, got ads last week with 50 brands at rollout and agency partnerships with WPP and Omnicom; a self-serve ad manager for Indian marketers opens Sept. 4 with a ₹725 ($7.60) daily minimum budget.
key_facts.excerpt: The company launched ads in India last week, one of ChatGPT's largest markets by weekly active users, with 50 brands participating at rollout and partnerships with agencies WPP and Omnicom. A self-serve ad manager for Indian marketers is set to open Sept. 4, with a daily minimum budget of ₹725 ($7.60).

stories.headline: OpenClaw ships 2.0, its biggest release: 16,000 PRs, shared cloud sessions, rebuilt memory

key_facts.fact: OpenClaw released version 2026.8.1, branded 'OpenClaw 2.0', built by 933 contributors including 569 first-timers and composed of more than 16,000 pull requests — the largest update in the open-source agent project's history.
key_facts.excerpt: Today we released by far the largest update in the history of OpenClaw. It was built by 933 contributors, including 569 first-time contributors, and is composed of over 16,000 pull requests.

key_facts.fact: The release started as two narrow jobs — simplifying installation and rebuilding the browser app — and grew into an overhaul touching installation, messaging, memory, skills, models, automations, browser and native apps, plugins and security.
key_facts.excerpt: We started by simplifying installation and rebuilding the browser app as a first-class experience, but doing that properly meant carrying the cleanup through the rest of OpenClaw until it became OpenClaw 2.0.

key_facts.fact: Shared cloud sessions turn OpenClaw into a multiplayer tool: a second person can join or take over a live agent session with the accumulated context intact, something the previous version could not do.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenClaw had no way to bring another team member into the work without losing what the Claw already knew. Shared cloud sessions changed that and turned OpenClaw into a multiplayer experience our team now uses to build OpenClaw.

key_facts.fact: The 16,000 pull requests amount to roughly half of all changes ever merged into the project, which paused its usual rapid release cadence for the drop.
key_facts.excerpt: According to the development team, OpenClaw 2.0 contains more than 16,000 pull requests from 933 contributors, 569 of them first-timers. That amounts to roughly half of all changes ever merged into the project.

key_facts.fact: Session transcripts moved from file-backed storage to a SQLite database, enabling full-text search over past conversations; sessions can also leave the local gateway and run on paired devices or cloud workers with the workspace travelling along.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the hood, session transcripts move from file-backed storage into a SQLite database, which speeds up loading history. ... Sessions can leave the local gateway and execute on paired devices or cloud workers, with the session workspace travelling along.

key_facts.fact: New memory architecture adds 'Active Memory' (recall from the same agent's past sessions) and 'Grounded Dreaming' (background processing of history into long-term memory); founder Peter Steinberger said a duplicate memory system was removed, cutting roughly 50,000 lines of code.
key_facts.excerpt: Core changes in 2.0 include Active Memory and Grounded Dreaming rebuilding the memory architecture ... Project founder Peter Steinberger revealed the new version removed a duplicate Memory system, cutting roughly 50,000 lines of code and keeping only a unified architecture.

key_facts.fact: Within hours of release users reported upgrade failures, including a boot loop on an M4 Pro at 100% CPU; the team acknowledged migration issues and said it is preparing further patches.
key_facts.excerpt: Within hours of release, someone on Reddit posted 'I let it upgrade itself and it died,' and another user reported OpenClaw entering a boot loop on an M4 Pro with CPU usage at 100%. ... The team has also acknowledged discovering migration issues and is preparing to continue patching.

key_facts.fact: Official performance figures from a simulated test environment show JavaScript requests dropping from 140 to 45 and startup time falling from about 1.6 seconds to 575 milliseconds.
key_facts.excerpt: Official performance figures come from a simulated test environment (mocked Gateway, 50ms HTTP/1.1 latency): JavaScript requests dropped from 140 to 45, and startup time fell from roughly 1.6 seconds to 575 milliseconds.

stories.headline: EU designates ChatGPT a Very Large Online Search Engine under the Digital Services Act

key_facts.fact: On August 31, 2026 the European Commission designated ChatGPT as a Very Large Online Search Engine (VLOSE), and Reddit and Roblox as Very Large Online Platforms (VLOPs), under the Digital Services Act.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, the Commission has designated ChatGPT as a Very Large Online Search Engine (VLOSE), as well as Reddit and Roblox as Very Large Online Platforms (VLOPs), under the Digital Services Act (DSA).

key_facts.fact: Each service declared it reaches at least 45 million average monthly users in the EU, the threshold that triggers designation.
key_facts.excerpt: These services declared that they reach at least 45 million average monthly users in the EU and thus meet the threshold for designation.

key_facts.fact: The three services get four months to comply with extra obligations: assessing and mitigating risks from illegal content, protecting minors' physical and mental health, and curbing risks to fundamental rights, electoral processes and public safety.
key_facts.excerpt: The three designated services have been granted a four-month grace period to comply with requirements including assessing and mitigating risks of illegal content dissemination and reducing adverse impacts on the mental and physical health of minors and users. They are also obligated to curb risks to fundamental rights, electoral processes, and public safety.

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT was classified as a search engine rather than a platform because the Commission recognised its AI-generated answers as an information-retrieval function; Reddit and Roblox were designated as platforms hosting third-party content.
key_facts.excerpt: ChatGPT was classified as an 'online search engine' under the DSA. The service developed by U.S.-based OpenAI, which generates AI responses to user queries, was recognized for its function as an information retrieval tool. Meanwhile, Reddit and Roblox were designated as 'online platforms' that enable the publication of third-party content.

key_facts.fact: Designation adds the services to a group of roughly two dozen platforms carrying the DSA's heaviest obligations, a list that already includes Meta, X, Amazon, TikTok, WhatsApp, YouTube and Google Search.
key_facts.excerpt: The tag is not a trophy. It adds ChatGPT and Roblox to a list of around two dozen platforms carrying the DSA's heaviest obligations. That group already runs from Meta and X to Amazon and TikTok. They get four months from designation to comply.

key_facts.fact: Designated services must set up risk-management systems, undergo external audits and provide data access, and the Commission can fine them for violations.
key_facts.excerpt: Services exceeding 45 million monthly users are classified as 'Very Large' and face stricter requirements than usual, including establishing risk management systems, undergoing external audits, and providing data access. ... The European Commission holds the authority to impose fines for violations.

stories.headline: Z.ai revenue quadruples to $142M but misses estimates by 29% as China's AI price war bites

key_facts.fact: Z.ai reported first-half 2026 revenue of 953.89 million yuan (about $142 million), up roughly 400% year on year, in its first interim report as a listed company.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese artificial intelligence company Z.ai on Monday reported a 400 per cent increase in first-half revenue ... Revenue for the six months ended June 30 rose to 953.89 million yuan (US$142 million).

key_facts.fact: The figure fell about 29% short of the 1.35 billion yuan analysts had projected on average, with China's AI price war against DeepSeek and Moonshot AI cited as the main cause.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue for the six months through June rose to 954 million yuan (US$142 million ...), falling short of an average analyst projection of 1.35 billion yuan.

key_facts.fact: Total loss for the half narrowed 12.1% to 2.07 billion yuan while R&D spending rose 33.6% to 2.13 billion yuan — more than the company's entire revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: Total loss for the six months ended June 30 narrowed 12.1 per cent to 2.07 billion yuan ... Research and development expenses rose 33.6 per cent to 2.13 billion yuan as Z.ai – known domestically as Zhipu AI – continued to invest aggressively in computing power and base model performance.

key_facts.fact: Growth came almost entirely from cloud-based deployment services, where revenue jumped 2,736% year on year to 825 million yuan from 29 million yuan; open-platform and API services now account for 86.5% of sales.
key_facts.excerpt: Top-line performance in the first half was primarily driven by cloud-based deployment services, where revenue jumped 2,736 per cent year on year to 825 million yuan from 29 million yuan.

key_facts.fact: Shares closed up 9.63% at HK$1,195 on Monday ahead of the results, still about 60% below the record HK$2,980 hit in June when market capitalisation briefly approached HK$1 trillion (US$127.5 billion).
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of Hong Kong-listed Z.ai closed up 9.63 per cent at HK$1,195 on Monday ahead of the [results]. The stock remains down about 60 per cent from its record high of HK$2,980 reached in June, when the company's market capitalisation briefly approached HK$1 trillion (US$127.5 billion).

key_facts.fact: At roughly $71.4 billion of market value against $141.8 million of half-year revenue, Z.ai trades at a price-to-sales ratio of about 252 on annualised revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: On the Hong Kong exchange, Z.ai currently carries a market capitalization of 556.42 billion Hong Kong dollars, which works out to roughly $71.4 billion ... Measured against half-year revenue of $141.8 million, that is a ratio of about 503 to 1, or a price-to-sales ratio of roughly 252 when the half year is annualized.

key_facts.fact: Rival MiniMax, which listed in Hong Kong a day after Z.ai, reported first-half revenue up 283.1% to $116 million over the same week.
key_facts.excerpt: MiniMax, Z.AI's closest rival for Hong Kong investor attention, posted a different kind of report the same week. The company said first-half revenue rose 283.1% to $116 [million].

key_facts.fact: Z.ai management said its models advanced from basic code suggestions to autonomous engineering and cybersecurity work, and claimed top-tier scores on the CyberGym and ExploitGym benchmarks with its Cybersecurity Co-work product.
key_facts.excerpt: Management highlighted a major shift in its AI model capabilities from simple code suggestions to full engineering project delivery ... The company also advanced in cybersecurity applications with its Cybersecurity Co-work offering, achieving top-tier scores on industry benchmarks like CyberGym and ExploitGym.

stories.headline: Anthropic signs users out of Claude after infostealer malware hijacks login sessions

key_facts.fact: Anthropic began warning Claude users on August 30, 2026 that infostealer malware on their own PCs stole active Claude login sessions, letting attackers access accounts and consume their usage.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic is warning some Claude users that infostealer malware on their PCs has stolen active Claude login sessions, allowing attackers to access accounts and consume their usage.

key_facts.fact: The company is signing affected users out, removing saved payment methods and refunding charges it identifies as unauthorized.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is signing affected users out of Claude, removing saved payment methods, and refunding charges it identifies as unauthorized.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic told an affected user: 'We have recently become aware of a bad actor that is using common infostealer malware to steal Claude login sessions from people's computers, then using those login sessions to access Claude accounts and consume their usage.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We have recently become aware of a bad actor that is using common infostealer malware to steal Claude login sessions from people's computers, then using those login sessions to access Claude accounts and consume their usage," Anthropic said in an email sent to an affected user, who shared it on Reddit.

key_facts.fact: The telltale sign of compromise is usage limits that appear to refill and then drain while the account owner isn't using Claude.
key_facts.excerpt: "If your usage limits looked like they refilled and then drained while you weren't using Claude, this was likely the cause," Anthropic warned.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic stressed the malware is general-purpose and unrelated to Claude or its infrastructure: it typically arrives via unofficial downloads or malicious apps and copies saved passwords, browser cookies and local app credentials, of which the Claude session was one item.
key_facts.excerpt: "We have no reason to believe that this malware is related to Claude, installed through Claude, or related to anything you did with Claude. It's general-purpose malware that typically arrives with an unofficial download or a malicious app, and it quietly copies saved passwords, login cookies in browsers, and credentials for other apps running locally."

key_facts.fact: Because a stolen session cookie is an already-completed login, two-factor authentication does not block the attacker; Anthropic warned that signing users out stops the stolen sessions but does not remove the malware, so the next login could be stolen the same way.
key_facts.excerpt: "Signing you out of Claude stops the stolen sessions, but it doesn't remove the malware," Anthropic warned. "If it's still on your computer, your next login session could be stolen the same way."

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said its own systems detected the unusual account activity; phones and tablets do not appear to have been involved, and the investigation is ongoing with no figure disclosed for accounts affected.
key_facts.excerpt: "Our systems detected this activity on your account, and we've therefore removed your card on file and signed out the sessions involved to help block further unauthorized access. Our investigation is [ongoing]. Our findings to [date suggest computers were] likely infected with infostealer malware, and may have been [infected for] some time. Phones and tablets do not appear to have been involved."

stories.headline: Together AI signs 250MW Saudi compute deal with Humain, citing US data-center backlash

key_facts.fact: San Francisco-based Together AI announced on Monday, August 31, 2026 a partnership with Humain, Saudi Arabia's state-backed AI company, giving it access to 250 megawatts from data centers inside the kingdom.
key_facts.excerpt: San Francisco-based tech startup Together AI announced on Monday that it's partnering with Humain, the Saudi Arabian AI company founded last year by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. The deal will give Together AI access to 250 megawatts of electricity from data centers located inside Saudi Arabia.

key_facts.fact: Together AI told the New York Times the 250MW partnership is expected to generate about $5 billion in annualized revenue and will nearly triple the company's computing capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: San Francisco-based Together AI announced an agreement on Monday with Humain, Saudi Arabia's state-backed AI company, to build a 250 megawatt data center in the kingdom. The partnership is expected to rake in $5 billion annually, Together AI told the New York Times. ... In brokering a deal with Humain, Together AI will nearly triple its computing capacity.

key_facts.fact: CEO and cofounder Vipul Prakash said local opposition is constraining US capacity: 'More and more, local communities don't want data centers in their backyards, and there are a lot of cancellations and moratoriums, so U.S. capacity is becoming even more constrained.'
key_facts.excerpt: "More and more, local communities don't want data centers in their backyards, and there are a lot of cancellations and moratoriums, so U.S. capacity is becoming even more constrained," Vipul Prakash, Together AI's CEO and cofounder, told the New York Times in a report published Monday.

key_facts.fact: Together AI, founded in 2022, runs cloud infrastructure for training and serving open-source AI models and says its platform is used by more than 1 million developers; under the deal customers can run workloads on infrastructure inside Saudi Arabia.
key_facts.excerpt: Together AI provides cloud computing services that allow companies and developers to train and operate open-source AI models. Founded in 2022, the company says its platform is used by more than 1 million developers. Under the Saudi partnership, customers will be able to use Together AI's platform while running their workloads on infrastructure located in the kingdom.

key_facts.fact: Humain already has partnerships with AWS, xAI (now SpaceXAI) and, as of last week, Microsoft; the same Monday it announced a deal with Applied Intuition to deploy thousands of autonomous trucks across Saudi logistics corridors by 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: Humain has additional partnerships with AWS, xAI (now SpaceXAI), and—as of last week—Microsoft. The Saudi Arabian AI company has also signed a deal with American startup Applied Intuition, aimed at "deploying thousands of autonomous trucks across key Saudi logistics corridors by 2030," according to a press release published Monday.

key_facts.fact: Prakash said the company will keep looking overseas because 'there's probably more international capacity that gets built than in the U.S.'
key_facts.excerpt: Prakash said the company will continue to look overseas to expand its data centers because "there's probably more international capacity that gets built than in the U.S."

stories.headline: OpenAI starts letting big customers pay only when its AI finishes the task

key_facts.fact: The Information reported on Monday, August 31, 2026 that OpenAI has recently begun allowing some major customers to pay only when its AI completes assigned tasks, a break from conventional usage-based pricing.
key_facts.excerpt: The Information reported on Monday, citing its sources, that OpenAI has recently started allowing some major customers to pay only when its AI completes assigned tasks, marking a shift away from conventional usage-based pricing.

key_facts.fact: Outcome-based pricing charges for the result rather than tokens, queries or compute time, giving providers an incentive to sell the outcome itself.
key_facts.excerpt: Rather than charging customers based on tokens, queries or computing time, outcome-based pricing gives providers an incentive to sell the result itself.

key_facts.fact: Salesforce is testing the same model for its Agentforce enterprise AI platform, letting customers pay based on results such as extra revenue from AI-assisted sales or savings from automated customer service.
key_facts.excerpt: Salesforce is now testing outcome-based pricing. This means the firm is letting some businesses pay for its enterprise AI platform, Agentforce, based on the results it delivers. For instance, customers could pay based on extra revenue from AI-assisted sales or savings from automated customer service.

key_facts.fact: The shift threatens 25 years of SaaS pricing convention, under which firms pay a flat per-seat fee for access regardless of performance — a model strained as agents let businesses use software with fewer employees.
key_facts.excerpt: The move could also upend 25 years of Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) pricing, in which firms pay a flat fee just to access a model, no matter how well it performs. ... But with AI agents able to complete tasks on their own, businesses may need fewer employees to interact with the software.

key_facts.fact: Other vendors are already there: Sierra and Fin charge on successful task completion, and Cognition has offered up to $10 million in credits if its technology fails to deliver what customers paid for.
key_facts.excerpt: Other AI companies are also trying similar pricing models. Sierra and Fin charge customers when their AI successfully completes tasks. Cognition, an AI software company, has also offered up to $10 million in credits if its technology fails to deliver results that match what customers paid for.

key_facts.fact: Salesforce's precedent is the Agentforce Help Agent launched in June 2026 at a flat $2 per autonomous resolution, with no charge if the customer requests a human or abandons the interaction unsatisfied.
key_facts.excerpt: Salesforce has launched Agentforce Help Agent ... customers will only pay, under a new pricing model, when it resolves a customer issue without human intervention. The price is a flat $2 per autonomous resolution. ... If a customer requests a human agent or abandons the interaction unsatisfied, there is no charge.

key_facts.fact: The pricing experiment comes as OpenAI prepares to launch Astra, its next-generation model aimed at AI agents.
key_facts.excerpt: The pricing shift comes as OpenAI gears up to launch Astra, its next-gen model focused on AI agents.
